title: Component Anatomy 🧬
description: Explore every part of the @Component decorator and how to create components from scratch.

slides.title: The Heart of Every Angular UI ❤️
slides.content:
# What is a Component?

A component is a TypeScript class that controls a patch of the screen called a **view**.

* It’s decorated with `@Component` to tell Angular how to build and render it.
* Every component has:
  - A **selector** (custom HTML tag).
  - A **template** (the view).
  - **Styles** (optional, scoped to the component).
  - The class itself (the logic).

Think of it as a custom HTML element with superpowers 💪.

slides.title: The Selector – Your Custom HTML Tag 🏷️
slides.content:
The `selector` property defines the HTML tag that represents the component. * Usually prefixed with `app-` to avoid name collisions (e.g., `app-header`). * It can be a tag, attribute, or class – but tags are most common. slides.title: Template vs templateUrl
slides.content: You can define the view inline or in a separate file.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use templateUrl for Cleaner Code

When your template has more than 3 lines, move it to an external HTML file. It keeps your TypeScript file clean and enables HTML editor features like autocompletion and syntax highlighting.

slides.title: Styles – Component‑Scoped CSS 🎨
slides.content:
By default, styles written in a component apply only to that component’s template. They won’t leak out.

* `styles: ['p { font-size: 20px; }']` – inline styles.
* `styleUrls: ['./my.component.css']` – external stylesheet.

This is called **View Encapsulation** – we’ll explore it more later in this chapter.

quizData.question: If a component has selector: 'app-nav', how would you use it in a parent template?
quizData.explanation: A tag selector like 'app-nav' is used as a custom HTML tag.

slides.title: Creating a Component with the CLI 🛠️
slides.content:
The Angular CLI makes creating components effortless:

```bash
ng generate component my-component
# shorthand: ng g c my-component
```

It will:
* Create a folder with 4 files (.ts, .html, .css, .spec.ts).
* Register the component in the nearest module’s `declarations`.
* Generate the boilerplate code for you.

Now you’re ready to start building!
